title: Running an alteration service: tags, minutes and fair prices

say: Running an alteration service: tags, minutes and fair prices.
This is the video for module 5 of Fashion Basics and Clothing Alterations.
You may have 20 or 30 garments in the workshop at once. Five pairs of black trousers, three gowns in the same lace. One mix-up can lose a client and cost you the price of the item.

panel.heading: Many small jobs need a system
items: Never lose or mix up a garment
Promise only dates you can keep
Price from the time a job really takes

say: So you need a simple counter system, a way to know how much work you can accept, and prices that follow the work.

panel.heading: Many small jobs need a system
items: Never lose or mix up a garment
Promise only dates you can keep

say: Pin a numbered tag to the garment, and write the same number on the job slip and in your job book.

panel.heading: Five things for every garment
items: Tag it with a number, for example 0127
Write the job slip with exact amounts
Photograph it, including existing damage
Empty the pockets in front of her
Give her a copy of the slip

say: The slip carries her name and phone, every alteration with exact amounts, the price, the deposit and the collection date.

say: Time your jobs for two or three weeks, and write the minutes on each slip. For example, Rukayat in Ilorin can sew about 5 hours a day, 6 days a week. That is 30 hours.

Already 30 minutes over: no new gown

say: She keeps half free for fittings, buying supplies and jobs that take longer than planned. That leaves 900 minutes.

say: Many alterers price by guessing, or copy the shop next door. That leads to cheap prices on slow, difficult jobs. Start instead with an hourly rate.
Esther wants to take home about 150,000 naira a month.
Her thread, needles, zips, fuel, data and transport cost about 30,000.
So she needs 180,000. Only count hours you can sell. 20 days of 5 hours is 100 hours. 180,000 divided by 100 is 1,800 naira an hour, or 30 naira a minute.
Price equals minutes, times your rate per minute, times a difficulty factor, plus materials. Then round it. A plain trouser hem of 30 minutes, at 30 naira a minute, is 900, rounded to 1,000 naira.

panel.heading: Minutes, rate, difficulty, materials
items: Trouser hem, 30 minutes: 1,000
Jeans, original hem, 45 minutes: 1,500
Waist take-in, 75 minutes: 2,500
Lace gown hem, 240 minutes, 1.5: 11,000

say: Jeans with the original hem take 45 minutes, so 1,500. A waist take-in of 75 minutes, 2,500.

panel.heading: Minutes, rate, difficulty, materials
items: Trouser hem, 30 minutes: 1,000

Lace gown hem, 240 minutes, 1.5: 11,000

say: A lined lace gown hem takes 240 minutes, with a difficulty factor of 1.5 for the risk. That is about 11,000 naira. It looks like just a hem, but it takes eight times as long.

say: The fabric is ordinary cotton, so the difficulty factor is 1.0.
50 minutes at 30 naira a minute is 1,500.
She supplies the new zip, about 500 naira.
The price is 2,000 naira. If the client wants it the same day and Esther must move another job, she adds a rush charge of 50 percent of the labour, 750 naira, making 2,750.
At collection, let her try on fitted work, and fix small issues on the spot if you can.

say: Send a polite reminder when it is ready, and again after a week. Write your rule for uncollected items on the slip at intake, so she agrees to it.

say: Keep your job book out of sight, and never post her garment or measurements without asking.

say: Fake transfer alerts and edited screenshots are common. Check the money has arrived in your own bank or wallet app before you hand anything over.

panel.rule: Confirm payment in your own app, never from a screenshot.

say: To remember. Tag, slip and photograph every garment. Plan in minutes and keep spare time. Build your rate from income and costs over billable hours. Charge for rush work, take deposits on gowns and restyles, and confirm payment before you release.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Tag, slip, photograph, empty pockets, copy
Plan in minutes, keep spare time
Rate = (income + costs) ÷ billable hours
Charge for rush work, take deposits
Confirm payment before release
